transcript.content: Hello. I'm a psychiatrist, and I'm here to help you today. What brings you in to see me?

I spend so much time checking and trying to fix this one thing about how I look that it’s taking over my day and costing me work. I'm just so overwhelmed because it feels like it's completely ruling my life right now.

Is this worry and checking behavior strictly focused on this specific aspect of your appearance, or do you also experience repetitive thoughts and behaviors about other things, like germs, safety, or order?

No, it's strictly about my appearance—I don't have any worries or rituals around germs, safety, or keeping things in order. My mind is completely consumed by how old and worn-out my face looks, specifically the deep lines and the gray at my temples. That is the only thing I'm constantly checking and trying to fix.
Do other people tell you that these lines and gray hair are normal or hardly noticeable, even though you find them deeply distressing or abnormal?

Yes, people tell me they barely even notice it, but I just can't accept that. I still feel incredibly distressed and constantly worry that they are secretly judging me or comparing me to my ex-wife's younger boyfriend and my polished clients.
Aside from your concerns about your appearance, do you often worry that you might be suffering from a serious, undetected physical illness?

No, I don't worry about having a physical illness at all. My anxiety is strictly focused on my appearance and how old my face looks. Physically I'm fine, it's just this one thing that completely consumes me.
How long have you been experiencing these intense worries and checking behaviors regarding your appearance?

It really started escalating about three years ago around the time of my divorce, especially after my ex-wife started dating a younger partner and friends made comments about me aging. Since then, it has gotten progressively worse over the last couple of years to the point where it is completely taking over.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a severe preoccupation with perceived defects in his physical appearance (deep lines and gray hair on his face) that are normal or barely noticeable to others. This preoccupation leads to excessive repetitive behaviors (checking and trying to fix his appearance) and causes significant distress and occupational impairment. In ICD-10, Body Dysmorphic Disorder (non-delusional dysmorphophobia) is classified under F45.2 (Hypochondriacal disorder). Other conditions like OCD and illness anxiety were ruled out.
